options: A backup if the camera breaks
questions.explain: The large one is for acquisition from altitude, the small one for the last meter, when the large one doesn't fit in the frame.

questions.q: The time_usec field in LANDING_TARGET should contain:
options: The time the message was sent
questions.explain: The autopilot matches the measurement against the position history at the moment of the frame.
0 is land, 1 is retry (default), 2 is hover.

questions.q: Below PLND_ALT_MIN, on target loss the vehicle:
questions.explain: Near the ground the camera often can't see the marker; finishing the landing is safer.

questions.q: In PX4, Required mode (MAV_CMD_NAV_LAND param2 = 2) with no target:
options: Searches for the target at PLD_SRCH_ALT
Does a normal landing right away

questions.q: The vehicle flies a spiral over the target. The first thing to check:
questions.explain: Move the target north in SITL: the vehicle should go north.

options: A Kalman filter on the target
questions.explain: 0 is raw, 1 is the Kalman filter.

questions.q: To convert angle_x/angle_y to meters, in practice the autopilot needs:
options: A second GPS for phase difference
questions.explain: Meters = altitude × tan(angle); baro altitude near the ground won't do.

questions.q: The vehicle ignores the target, and the GCS messages show “Plnd: Frame not supported”. What is the companion sending?
questions.fragment:
LANDING_TARGET time_usec=1234567 target_num=0 frame=1 (MAV_FRAME_LOCAL_NED)
               angle_x=0.05 angle_y=-0.02 distance=6.1
options: An unsupported coordinate frame: ArduPilot accepts only MAV_FRAME_BODY_FRD or LOCAL_FRD
angle_x = 0.05 rad is outside the camera's field of view, so the target is dropped
time_usec must match the autopilot boot time, otherwise ArduPilot drops such a message
distance must be 0 in the angle version, otherwise the target is considered invalid
questions.explain: ArduPilot's LANDING_TARGET handler rejects other frames and prints this message.
